reasoning_summary: The run's internal statistics look clean. It has 12 stationary cycles, a drag drift of 0.00018797, a drag 95% CI of 5.8758e-05, and max Courant number 0.38878. The inlet is uniform and blockage is 0.0125. Statistical convergence is therefore not the problem.

The mesh is very coarse for a vortex-shedding wake. It has only 7616 cells, a representative cell size of 0.91664 D, 56 streamwise wake cells, and a last wake cell of 2.0173 D. A cell of about one diameter or more cannot resolve the shed vortices. Together with linearUpwind convection, this probably adds numerical dissipation that shifts the shedding frequency and the wake-dependent mean drag.

The wall-adjacent resolution is also modest: 80 cells around the cylinder, with max non-orthogonality 41.56 deg and skewness 0.51811. The 3% tolerance on both Cd and St needs a demonstrated mesh-converged wake.

The St uncertainty is not shown to be below 3%. The stated strouhal_frequency_resolution is 0.013333, about 8.6% of the reported St of 0.15561. Any sub-bin precision comes from interpolation or cycle counting, which this evidence does not validate.

The evidence contains only one run, with no mesh or time-step refinement and no independent reference. The reported Cd of 1.2951 and St of 0.15561 are therefore unverified for discretisation error. The tight statistical metrics only show the run is self-consistent. The coarse wake mesh makes the 3% accuracy unlikely, so I reject.
